sentences.en: Current Challenges Confronting U.S. Higher Education.
sentences.zh: 当前美国高等教育面临的挑战。
sentences.asr_text: Current Challenges Confronting U.S. Higher Education
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In our last lecture, we discussed challenges that face universities and colleges worldwide.
sentences.zh: 上节课，我们讨论了世界各地大学和学院所面临的挑战。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Today we'll take a special look at U.S. higher education and see what challenges U.S. higher education is facing.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将重点看看美国高等教育，了解它正在面临哪些挑战。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK, let’s get started.
sentences.zh: 好，我们开始吧。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The first challenge we are examining in today’s lecture is the force of the marketplace on higher education.
sentences.zh: 今天讲座中，我们首先要考察的挑战，是市场力量对高等教育的影响。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Many people believe that the marketplace has overtaken state government as the dominant external force shaping and reshaping American higher education, even for public colleges and universities.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为，市场已经取代州政府，成为塑造和重塑美国高等教育的主导性外部力量，即使对于公立大学和学院也是如此。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: You may ask, why is it so?
sentences.zh: 你可能会问，为什么会这样呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Well, as is always the case, government support is not keeping pace with educational expenditures.
sentences.zh: 事情往往就是这样：政府的支持跟不上教育开支的增长。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So in many ways, the market is having more bearing on higher education than government.
sentences.zh: 所以，在很多方面，市场对高等教育的影响比政府更大。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In order to create more flexibility, many public colleges and universities are now asking for less government regulation and supervision.
sentences.zh: 为了获得更多灵活性，许多公立大学和学院现在要求减少政府的管制和监督。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In some instances, they are even asking for less state money in return for more autonomy.
sentences.zh: 有时，他们甚至愿意少拿一些州政府经费，以换取更多自主权。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And their argument is that the current structures and accountability requirements have hindered their capacity to be effective and efficient.
sentences.zh: 他们的理由是，现有的组织结构和问责要求，妨碍了他们有效、高效地运作。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The ability to set their own tuition fees and secure freedom from state policies and regulations in areas such as purchasing and building represent just some of the additional autonomy that public institutions are seeking.
sentences.zh: 自行决定学费、在采购和建设等领域摆脱州政府政策与规章的约束，只是公立院校正在争取的额外自主权中的一部分。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And many are pressing for new legislation to provide this freedom through a range of innovations, including public corporations, charter colleges, state enterprise status, and performance contracts.
sentences.zh: 许多院校还在推动新的立法，通过一系列制度创新来保障这种自由，包括公营法人、特许学院、州属企业地位和绩效合同。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So what is the result of these efforts?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些努力带来了什么结果呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Well, the result is that activities and research in certain fields and disciplines, for example, engineering, applied natural science, and agricultural science, become higher institutional priorities because they have stronger market value than other programs such as humanities do.
sentences.zh: 结果是，工程、应用自然科学和农业科学等某些领域和学科的活动与研究，在院校内部被置于更优先的位置，因为它们比人文学科等专业具有更高的市场价值。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So what has happened is that institutions create new programs, alter academic calendars, and pursue different financial aid policies to capture more and better students — in particular those who can afford to pay high tuition.
sentences.zh: 因此，院校开设新项目、调整校历，并采取不同的助学政策，以吸引更多、更优秀的学生，尤其是那些有能力支付高额学费的学生。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For instance, executive MBA programs are increasingly popular.
sentences.zh: 例如，高级管理人员工商管理硕士项目越来越受欢迎。

w.m: n.高级管理人员工商管理硕士项目

sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Also, institutions seek contracts and partnership agreements, and enhance research programs with practical applications that have large financial payouts.
sentences.zh: 此外，院校还会争取合同和合作协议，并加强具有实际应用价值、能带来可观经济回报的研究项目。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In order to do so, they are changing their institutional structures.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这些，他们正在改变院校的组织结构。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And how do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们具体是怎么做的呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Let me tell you.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Institutions would add new units that focus on generating external grants and bringing new technology to market.
sentences.zh: 院校会增设新部门，专门争取外部资助，并推动新技术进入市场。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: They would build conference centers and create for-profit subsidiaries.
sentences.zh: 他们会建设会议中心，并设立营利性附属机构。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: All these are done to generate more revenue for institutions.
sentences.zh: 这些做法都是为了给院校创造更多收入。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: What are the implications of this?
sentences.zh: 这会带来什么影响呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Well, the implications are that academic research is increasingly focused on marketable knowledge, entrepreneurial priorities are taking precedence, services are being outsourced, and students are carrying an increasing burden to pay higher tuition fees for their education.
sentences.zh: 其影响是，学术研究越来越注重可出售、符合市场需求的知识，创业和经营方面的考量被放在优先位置，服务被外包，而学生则承担着越来越重的高额学费负担。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Then how do university administrators view this trend?
sentences.zh: 那么，大学管理者如何看待这一趋势呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: That is, the marketplace is showing stronger impact on how institutions are run.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，市场对院校运作方式的影响正在增强。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In fact, university administrators see little option except to respond to the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大学管理者认为，除了回应市场，他们几乎没有其他选择。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The reason is, if their institution does not react effectively, it will not have the necessary resources to offer high-quality and diverse academic programs.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果院校不能作出有效回应，就无法获得提供优质、多样化学术项目所需的资源。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Institutions unable to compete may face hard circumstances because government support continues to fall, students become better-informed consumers, and advances in technology also widen the number and reach of competitors.
sentences.zh: 无法参与竞争的院校可能面临困境，因为政府支持持续减少，学生作为消费者掌握的信息越来越充分，而技术进步也使竞争者数量增多、覆盖范围扩大。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In turn, the ability to compete — for students, resources, faculty and prestige — becomes a driving strategic force.
sentences.zh: 反过来，争夺学生、资源、师资和声望的竞争能力，就成了一股重要的战略推动力。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: At its extreme, competition can overtake more traditional academic values.
sentences.zh: 在极端情况下，竞争可能凌驾于较传统的学术价值之上。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: However, the downside of pursuing market goals without appropriately balancing them against the public good is... is that institutions will no longer be able to fulfill their social responsibility to produce well-educated citizens and face the threat of losing their privileged place in society as they resemble more closely other market-driven organizations.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果追求市场目标时不能恰当地兼顾公共利益，就会产生弊端：院校将无法履行培养受过良好教育的公民这一社会责任；而且，由于它们越来越像其他受市场驱动的组织，也将面临失去其在社会中优越地位的威胁。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now let’s move on to the second challenge facing U.S. higher education.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们谈美国高等教育面临的第二项挑战。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: That is the tension between competition and equality in admissions decisions.
sentences.zh: 这就是竞争与招生公平之间的矛盾。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Since World War II, U.S. higher education has been engaged in a process of “massification”, that is, expanding to serve students from all walks of life.
sentences.zh: 自第二次世界大战以来，美国高等教育一直在经历“大众化”的过程，也就是不断扩大规模，为各个社会阶层的学生提供教育。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Motivating this effort is a widespread belief in the power of education to create social and economic mobility and a belief in the morality and social value of making higher education accessible to everyone.
sentences.zh: 推动这一努力的是一种普遍信念：教育能够促进社会和经济地位的流动；同时，让每个人都能接受高等教育，也具有道德意义和社会价值。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Research data bear out public perceptions: When young people from low-income backgrounds complete a bachelor’s degree, their income and employment characteristics after graduation are equivalent to their peers from more affluent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 研究数据证实了公众的看法：来自低收入家庭的年轻人取得学士学位后，其毕业后的收入和就业情况，与来自较富裕家庭的同龄人相当。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So education can truly be “the great equalizer”.
sentences.zh: 所以，教育确实能够成为“促进平等的重要力量”。

w.m: n.使人处于平等地位的因素

sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Although there is widespread public faith in the value of higher education, the progress of massification has been slow and uneven.
sentences.zh: 尽管公众普遍相信高等教育的价值，大众化的进展却一直缓慢而且不均衡。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And why is it slow and uneven?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个过程既缓慢又不均衡呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Well, one, higher education did not admit significant numbers of racial and ethnic minorities until after the civil rights of the 1960s forced change.
sentences.zh: 首先，直到二十世纪六十年代的民权运动推动变革之后，高等院校才开始大量招收少数族裔学生。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Second, despite significant expenditures on financial aid, minority and low-income individuals are still less likely to attend college than whites or students from middle- and upper-income families.
sentences.zh: 其次，尽管投入了大量助学经费，少数族裔和低收入群体上大学的可能性，仍低于白人或中高收入家庭的学生。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Although access gaps have nowadays narrowed somewhat, large gaps remain between completion rates.
sentences.zh: 虽然如今入学机会方面的差距有所缩小，毕业完成率之间仍然存在很大差距。

w.m: n.完成学业的比例；毕业完成率

sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Low-income students come to college less prepared, and must balance academic demands with work and family responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 低收入学生入学时往往准备不足，而且必须在学业要求与工作、家庭责任之间取得平衡。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Finding ways to increase the enrollment rates of low-income students and encourage their success once enrolled are two of the most important problems facing American higher education.
sentences.zh: 如何提高低收入学生的入学率，并帮助他们在入学后顺利完成学业，是美国高等教育面临的两项重要问题。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: One of the challenges to meet these goals is that they can conflict with the other central tenets of American higher education.
sentences.zh: 实现这些目标的一项难题在于，它们可能与美国高等教育的其他核心原则产生冲突。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: That is market competition and resistance to government control, as I said before.
sentences.zh: 如前所述，这些原则就是市场竞争，以及对政府管制的抵制。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For example, institutional competition for the most academically talented students is likely to encourage increased use of tuition discounting for students who have no financial need, and this could divert resources away from low-income students who need financial aid.
sentences.zh: 例如，院校争夺学业表现最优秀学生的竞争，可能促使它们更多地向没有经济需要的学生提供学费优惠，从而把资源从真正需要经济资助的低收入学生身上转移走。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Similarly, institutions may seek to distinguish themselves in the academic marketplace by becoming more selective in admissions decisions, thus reducing the number of low-income students admitted.
sentences.zh: 同样，院校可能为了在高等教育市场中脱颖而出，在录取时提高选择性，进而减少被录取的低收入学生人数。

w.m: adj.有选择性的；筛选严格的

sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: However, a primary role of government is to mediate the potentially negative effects of competition by insisting that institutions adhere to their missions and that institutions provide need-based financial assistance to students.
sentences.zh: 然而，政府的一项主要职责，是调节竞争可能带来的负面影响，具体做法是坚持要求：院校坚守自身使命，并为学生提供以经济需要为依据的资助。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So a constant preoccupation of American higher education is this tension between the competitive, ambitious nature of institutions and the interests of government in promoting important public goals, primary among them broad access and widespread success for all students.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国高等教育始终关注着这样一种矛盾：一方面，院校具有竞争性和追求发展的雄心；另一方面，政府需要推动重要的公共目标，而其中首要的就是扩大入学机会，并让各类学生普遍取得成功。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For today’s lecture, we have briefly discussed some of the major challenges facing U.S. higher education, such as the impact of the marketplace on institutions and the tension between competition and promoting public goals.
sentences.zh: 在今天的讲座中，我们简要讨论了美国高等教育面临的一些主要挑战，例如市场对院校的影响，以及竞争和推动公共目标之间的矛盾。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
sentences.zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。
sentences.asr_text: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: This is the end of section A mini-lecture.
sentences.zh: A节短讲到此结束。
sentences.asr_text: This is the end of section A mini lecture.

在院校内部被置于更优先的位置，因为它们比人文学科等专业具有更高的市场价值。
manual_splits.evidence: 工程/应用自然科学/农业科学三个并列例子完整留首屏；后屏优先地位与市场价值原因同在。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: So what has happened is that institutions create new programs, alter academic calendars, and pursue different financial aid policies to capture more and better students — in particular those who can afford to pay high tuition.
zh: 因此，院校开设新项目、调整校历，
并采取不同的助学政策，以吸引更多、更优秀的学生，尤其是那些有能力支付高额学费的学生。
manual_splits.evidence: 助学政策对应第二屏pursue financial aid policies，不能提前与首屏programs/calendars同译。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Well, the implications are that academic research is increasingly focused on marketable knowledge, entrepreneurial priorities are taking precedence, services are being outsourced, and students are carrying an increasing burden to pay higher tuition fees for their education.
zh: 其影响是，学术研究越来越注重可出售、符合市场需求的知识，创业和经营方面的考量被放在优先位置，
服务被外包，而学生则承担着越来越重的高额学费负担。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Institutions unable to compete may face hard circumstances because government support continues to fall, students become better-informed consumers, and advances in technology also widen the number and reach of competitors.
zh: 无法参与竞争的院校可能面临困境，因为政府支持持续减少，
学生作为消费者掌握的信息越来越充分，而技术进步也使竞争者数量增多、覆盖范围扩大。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: However, the downside of pursuing market goals without appropriately balancing them against the public good is... is that institutions will no longer be able to fulfill their social responsibility to produce well-educated citizens and face the threat of losing their privileged place in society as they resemble more closely other market-driven organizations.
zh: 然而，如果追求市场目标时不能恰当地兼顾公共利益，就会产生弊端：
院校将无法履行培养受过良好教育的公民这一社会责任；
而且，由于它们越来越像其他受市场驱动的组织，也将面临失去其在社会中优越地位的威胁。
manual_splits.evidence: and与第二项失去社会优越地位威胁同留第三屏；两种弊端分配明确。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Since World War II, U.S. higher education has been engaged in a process of “massification”, that is, expanding to serve students from all walks of life.
zh: 自第二次世界大战以来，美国高等教育一直在经历“大众化”的过程，
也就是不断扩大规模，为各个社会阶层的学生提供教育。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Motivating this effort is a widespread belief in the power of education to create social and economic mobility and a belief in the morality and social value of making higher education accessible to everyone.
zh: 推动这一努力的是一种普遍信念：教育能够促进社会和经济地位的流动；
同时，让每个人都能接受高等教育，也具有道德意义和社会价值。
manual_splits.evidence: 第二种普遍可及性的道德/社会价值信念与and/同时放同屏。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Research data bear out public perceptions: When young people from low-income backgrounds complete a bachelor’s degree, their income and employment characteristics after graduation are equivalent to their peers from more affluent backgrounds.
zh: 研究数据证实了公众的看法：来自低收入家庭的年轻人取得学士学位后，
其毕业后的收入和就业情况，与来自较富裕家庭的同龄人相当。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Second, despite significant expenditures on financial aid, minority and low-income individuals are still less likely to attend college than whites or students from middle- and upper-income families.
zh: 其次，尽管投入了大量助学经费，
少数族裔和低收入群体上大学的可能性，仍低于白人或中高收入家庭的学生。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Finding ways to increase the enrollment rates of low-income students and encourage their success once enrolled are two of the most important problems facing American higher education.
manual_splits.at: are two of the most important
zh: 如何提高低收入学生的入学率，并帮助他们在入学后顺利完成学业，
是美国高等教育面临的两项重要问题。
manual_splits.evidence: 入学后once enrolled的成功条件与前屏enrollment/success完整同在；后屏只陈述两项问题的地位。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: For example, institutional competition for the most academically talented students is likely to encourage increased use of tuition discounting for students who have no financial need, and this could divert resources away from low-income students who need financial aid.
zh: 例如，院校争夺学业表现最优秀学生的竞争，
可能促使它们更多地向没有经济需要的学生提供学费优惠，
从而把资源从真正需要经济资助的低收入学生身上转移走。
manual_splits.evidence: 三屏按竞争、对无经济需要学生的学费优惠、资源转离低收入学生排列；修复旧切法英文与中文三屏整体错位。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: Similarly, institutions may seek to distinguish themselves in the academic marketplace by becoming more selective in admissions decisions, thus reducing the number of low-income students admitted.
zh: 同样，院校可能为了在高等教育市场中脱颖而出，在录取时提高选择性，
进而减少被录取的低收入学生人数。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: However, a primary role of government is to mediate the potentially negative effects of competition by insisting that institutions adhere to their missions and that institutions provide need-based financial assistance to students.
zh: 然而，政府的一项主要职责，是调节竞争可能带来的负面影响，具体做法是坚持要求：
院校坚守自身使命，并为学生提供以经济需要为依据的资助。
manual_splits.evidence: 政府调节负面影响及insisting为首屏；坚持使命和按经济需要资助两项要求同在次屏，中文保义调序。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: So a constant preoccupation of American higher education is this tension between the competitive, ambitious nature of institutions and the interests of government in promoting important public goals, primary among them broad access and widespread success for all students.
zh: 因此，美国高等教育始终关注着这样一种矛盾：一方面，院校具有竞争性和追求发展的雄心；
另一方面，政府需要推动重要的公共目标，
而其中首要的就是扩大入学机会，并让各类学生普遍取得成功。
manual_splits.evidence: competitive/ambitious两项共同修饰院校性质，完整留首屏；政府目标为第二屏；入学机会/各类学生成功为第三屏，不在competitive与ambitious之间割裂。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。
manual_splits.evidence_ref: 核验/长句语义分屏/2016—2019及2021-平表.json
manual_splits.approval_scope: 人工语义分屏；未核音频/最终截图，不含虚构时间。

manual_splits.en: For today’s lecture, we have briefly discussed some of the major challenges facing U.S. higher education, such as the impact of the marketplace on institutions and the tension between competition and promoting public goals.
zh: 在今天的讲座中，我们简要讨论了美国高等教育面临的一些主要挑战，
例如市场对院校的影响，以及竞争和推动公共目标之间的矛盾。
manual_splits.evidence: 逐屏核对英文主干、原因条件、列举对象与中文对应；当前自动方案自然，片段完整拼回当前中文。 中文片段literal拼回当前整句；只核语义，原音换屏须预检真实词首/停顿。

evidence.rationale: 局部错位上下文Parakeet恢复了完整实际词；独立Whisper文本互证（不借用公共模板补英语或估时）。

sentences.en: Maureen McLane is a poet and critic.
sentences.zh: 莫琳·麦克莱恩是一位诗人和评论家。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: After her undergraduate studies in American history and literature, she studied English literature on a scholarship before earning her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 她本科时学习美国历史和文学，随后获得奖学金学习英国文学，之后在芝加哥大学取得博士学位。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: In addition to academic publications on British romanticism, Maureen McLane has written a number of memoirs and criticism.
sentences.zh: 除了有关英国浪漫主义的学术著作，莫琳·麦克莱恩还写过一些回忆录和评论作品。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: One of them, My Poets, became a finalist for the 2012 National Book Critics Circle Award in autobiography.
sentences.zh: 其中一本《我的诗人》，入围了二〇一二年美国国家书评人协会奖的自传类奖项。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: And her most recent collection of poetry, This Blue, was a finalist for the 2014 National Book Award.
sentences.zh: 她最近出版的诗集《这片蓝》，也入围了二〇一四年美国国家图书奖。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Today, we have Maureen McLane, now professor of English at New York University, with us on the radio show.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们请到了现任纽约大学英语教授莫琳·麦克莱恩，做客本台广播节目。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Good evening, Maureen.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，莫琳。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Good evening!
sentences.zh: 晚上好！
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Now, can you tell us when you first began to read poetry?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们，您最早是什么时候开始读诗的吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I would probably say, in my high school days.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是在高中时期。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Of course, there had been some other things in the environment in my childhood before high school, like nursery rhymes, hymns, my mother’s playing piano and guitar, poems my father might come out with.
sentences.zh: 当然，在高中之前，我童年时的生活环境中也有其他相关事物，比如童谣、赞美诗、母亲弹奏钢琴和吉他，以及父亲随口念出的诗句。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: But in terms of reading poetry, it really came about through high school.
sentences.zh: 但是，真正开始阅读诗歌，还是在高中阶段。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Literature classes in general were very stimulating to me.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，文学课对我很有启发。

w.m: adj.富有启发的；激发兴趣的

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: You begin one section of My Poets by talking about the lecture course you took in your freshman year with Helen Vendler, and the poetry section you had with William Corbett.
sentences.zh: 在《我的诗人》的一个章节开头，您谈到了大一时上的海伦·文德勒的讲座课，以及威廉·科贝特教授的诗歌课。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Were there other teachers who were important to you?
sentences.zh: 还有其他对您很重要的老师吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Well, there were several people important to me who weren't poetry people at all — they were historians or professors of music.
sentences.zh: 对我很重要的几个人，完全不是诗歌界人士，而是历史学家或音乐教授。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Oh, that’s interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很有意思。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I had a wonderful tutor, now a professor of English at the University of Chicago, Janice Knight.
sentences.zh: 我有过一位很出色的导师，贾妮丝·奈特，她现在是芝加哥大学的英语教授。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Janice was and is a scholar of colonial America, but she also knew a lot about a certain line in American poetry.
sentences.zh: 贾妮丝过去和现在一直是一位研究殖民地时期美国的学者，但她也很熟悉美国诗歌的某一流派。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: She introduced me to Susan Howe’s work.
sentences.zh: 她让我接触到了苏珊·豪的作品。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I mean, those people became important to me in various ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人以不同的方式对我产生了重要影响。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I almost feel as if in the end the poets themselves are the most important teachers.
sentences.zh: 我几乎觉得，到头来，诗人本人就是最重要的老师。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I do think that if you bend towards becoming a writer, at the end of the day, it’s writing that teaches you, I mean, other writers’ works.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，如果你倾向于成为一名作家，归根结底，教会你写作的是写作本身；我是指其他作家的作品。

w.h: at the end of the day

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: You were an undergraduate at Harvard, and then you returned to teach there.
sentences.zh: 您在哈佛读过本科，后来又回到那里任教。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是一种怎样的体验？

w.m: prep.像……；此处询问情况或感受

sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: When I returned, I was at a very different phase of life.
sentences.zh: 回去的时候，我已处于人生中一个很不一样的阶段。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Being back as a professor, Cambridge, where Harvard University is, was very different — it was much more commercialized and cleaned-up than when I was an undergrad.
sentences.zh: 以教授的身份重返校园时，哈佛大学所在的剑桥市已经很不一样了：与我读本科时相比，那里商业化程度更高，环境也更整洁。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I liked being near Fresh Pond, and going to Walden.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢住在弗雷什池附近，也喜欢去瓦尔登。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I felt like I was getting to know New England a little bit better, in a way that was very different from when I was 18.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己更加了解新英格兰了，而这种了解方式与我十八岁时很不一样。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I liked that, and I was more aware of the environment,
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这种体验，也更加留意周围的环境。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: You write in My Poets about the power of listening to “poetry fans read those poems or works they are committed to.” Is this an important teaching tool for you? .
sentences.zh: 您在《我的诗人》中谈到了聆听诗歌爱好者朗读他们倾心的诗歌或作品所具有的力量。这对您来说是一种重要的教学工具吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I definitely bring recordings to class.
sentences.zh: 我一定会把录音带到课堂上。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Recordings offer a great way to refocus one’s attention on the poem.
sentences.zh: 录音是让人重新把注意力集中到诗歌上的一种很好的方式。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I feel like it’s definitely a zone for encounter, a zone that’s really powerful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这无疑是一个让人相遇、与诗歌接触的空间，是一个非常有力量的空间。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I also think there is an inner ear, which is much more relevant to my sense of poetry than actual vocalization.
sentences.zh: 我还认为存在一种“内在的听觉”，与实际发声相比，它和我对诗歌的感知更为相关。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Some people are very attuned to this ear.
sentences.zh: 有些人对这种内在听觉非常敏感。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: For example, they compose in their minds, maybe reciting aloud, and only at the end do they write things down.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们会先在脑中创作，也许会大声念出来，直到最后才把内容写下来。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: So, I do think there’s an inner ear that is activated when one writes.
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实认为，人在写作时，会激活一种内在听觉。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Or at least for me.
sentences.zh: 至少对我来说是这样。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: And that is as loud, as audible, as our conversation right now.
sentences.zh: 而且，它就像我们现在的交谈一样响亮、一样清晰可闻。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。

sentences.en: Now listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 现在请听访谈的第二部分。
sentences.asr_text: Now listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on part 2 of the interview.
sentences.zh: 第6至10题根据访谈的第二部分提问。
sentences.asr_text: Questions 6 to 10 are based on part 2 of the interview
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: In My Poets, you write about attending readings, and socializing with writers, and the energy or tension of those face-to-face encounters.
sentences.zh: 在《我的诗人》中，您写到了参加朗诵会、与作家交往，以及这些面对面接触带来的活力或紧张感。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: But in interviews, you've also said that you think that it’s “a tremendous gift to be lonely in poetry”.
sentences.zh: 但您在访谈中也说过，对诗歌创作而言，“孤独是一份极大的馈赠”。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Could you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这一点吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I really think this comes down to one’s temperament.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这归根结底取决于一个人的性情。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Other writers are much more readily sociable creatures.
sentences.zh: 其他作家往往更乐于社交。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: They feel there’s a kind of continuity between their writing life and their social life.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，写作生活与社交生活之间存在某种连续性。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I never experienced things that way at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全没有过那样的体验。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Could you tell us why?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们为什么吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: For me, poetry was not a zone about professionalization or networking.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，诗歌并不是一个以职业化或建立人脉为中心的领域。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: There are many, many different kinds of writerly engagement, but I feel that people should be given permission not to engage.
sentences.zh: 作家与外界互动的方式有很多很多种，但我觉得，人们也应该被允许不参与其中。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: There’s so much pressure to find a community, and one wants a community — but community may not come from the people organizing the poetry reading.
sentences.zh: 寻找一个群体的压力很大，人们也确实渴望有一个群体；但这个群体未必来自那些组织诗歌朗诵会的人。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: It might be found among the folk musicians playing down there in the street.
sentences.zh: 你也可能在街头演奏的民间音乐人那里找到这个群体。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: A community for poets is not necessarily other living poets.
sentences.zh: 诗人的群体不一定就是其他在世的诗人。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Another question.
sentences.zh: 换个问题。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: How do you arrange the poetry in your books?
sentences.zh: 您是怎样安排诗集中各首诗的顺序的？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I notice that they’re all divided into sections, and all end with a concluding part.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，它们都分成若干部分，而且最后都有一个结尾部分。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: My last two books, for instance, This Blue, have central sections that speak to a complex set of associations with particular places.
sentences.zh: 比如，我最近的两本书，包括《这片蓝》，都有位于中间的部分，涉及与特定地点相关的一组复杂联想。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: It’s also the case that some of the poems are so strongly voiced that if I were to begin with them.
sentences.zh: 有些诗的声音或表达方式又特别鲜明，以至于如果我拿它们作为开篇……

w.m: adj.具有某种声音或表达方式的

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: People might think the entire book is in that one mode, and I wanted to avoid that.
sentences.zh: 人们可能就会以为整本书都是那一种风格，而我想避免这种情况。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: And I often write sequences.
sentences.zh: 我还经常写组诗。

w.m: n.组诗；有顺序的一组作品

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: So I almost think of the sections more musically.
sentences.zh: 所以，我几乎是在从音乐的角度思考这些部分的。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Emm, Emm...
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯……
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: And I’m interested in ushering people through a series of mental and tonal landscapes, of sound- and thought-worlds.
sentences.zh: 我希望引导读者走过一系列精神与声调的景观，走过声音和思想的世界。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: For good or ill, my books have not tended to be that narrative.
sentences.zh: 不论这是好是坏，我的书一直都不太偏重叙事。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Is this the reason that each section has a concluding part?
sentences.zh: 这就是每个部分都设置结尾的原因吗？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: I think a concluding stanza marks a kind of “sending forth of the book” to the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为，结尾的一节诗标志着一种把这本书“送入世界”的方式。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: It also allows you to back away from something, to modulate out of certain kinds of intensities, and to gesture maybe to something in the future.
sentences.zh: 它还让你能够从某些东西中退后一步，从某种强烈的情绪中缓缓转出，并且也许向未来的某种事物作出示意。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: It can either restate a note, or it can refer to something more broadly.
sentences.zh: 它可以重申一个基调，也可以指向更广阔的内容。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Do you have a particular approach to reading your own poetry aloud?
sentences.zh: 您朗读自己的诗时，有没有某种特定的方法？
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Well, you can get locked into your own sense of things, and your way may not be the best way to read that poem.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被自己固有的理解束缚，而你的方式未必就是朗读那首诗的最佳方式。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: You can get a little muscular contraction on your face.
sentences.zh: 你的面部可能会出现一点肌肉收缩。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: One doesn’t want to have facial tics, one doesn’t want things to be routinized, and I think about that.
sentences.zh: 人们不希望自己出现面部抽动，也不希望一切都变成固定套路，我会思考这些问题。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Sometimes people are surprised by my reading.
sentences.zh: 有时候，人们会对我的朗读方式感到惊讶。
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: I remember a poet said to me, “Oh, your poems are a lot funnier than I thought they were.” He was being very nice, but I didn’t know how to take that!
sentences.zh: 我记得一位诗人对我说：“哦，你的诗比我想象的好笑多了。”他的态度很友善，但我当时不知道该怎么理解这句话！
sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: Ha ha ha...
sentences.zh: 哈哈哈……
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。
sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Maureen, thank you so much for being with us today.
sentences.zh: 莫琳，非常感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

w.m: phr.和我们在一起；参加我们的节目

sentences.speaker: M

sentences.en: Pleasure.
sentences.zh: 很荣幸。

w.m: n.荣幸；用作回应感谢的客气话

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.en: This is the end of part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。
sentences.asr_text: This is the end of part two of the interview.
